summary: The bill amends federal law governing Olympic sports to require national governing bodies to limit athlete participation in events to categories matching each athlete's biological sex (defined as immutable male or female status based on reproductive function at conception) and to continue sanctioning prior single-sex competitions.

scores.thoughts: The bill amends eligibility rules for Olympic sports governing bodies under title 36 USC but contains no provisions related to federal spending, appropriations, or budgets.
No provisions in the bill address taxes, tax policy, rates, or revenue measures.
The bill focuses exclusively on athletic eligibility criteria and contains nothing related to healthcare systems, coverage, or medical policy.
No references to firearms, gun regulations, or Second Amendment issues appear in the legislation.
The bill does not address immigration, border policy, visas, or related protections.
No content in the bill pertains to reproductive rights or abortion access.
The legislation contains no provisions affecting military or defense spending levels.
No environmental regulations, climate policy, or conservation measures are addressed.
The bill does not modify or reference welfare programs, food assistance, or other safety-net policies.
While the bill affects amateur athletic competitions that may occur in educational settings, it does not address school funding, curriculum, federal involvement in education, or school choice.
No provisions relate to drug enforcement, decriminalization, or controlled substances.
The bill does not touch on sentencing, policing, rehabilitation, or criminal justice reform.
No trade, tariffs, or globalization measures are present.
The legislation has no bearing on deficit spending or debt reduction strategies.

The bill mandates that national governing bodies require athletes to compete only in events matching their biological sex (defined at conception by reproductive function) for Olympic, Paralympic, and related sanctioned events. This directly restricts transgender athletes from participating in categories aligned with their gender identity, thereby limiting expansions of legal protections or inclusion policies for LGBTQ+ individuals in sports.
No provisions address foreign aid, international assistance, or related funding.
The bill contains nothing related to voting access, election integrity, or electoral processes.
No data privacy, technology regulation, or surveillance provisions are included.
The legislation does not address worker protections, union rights, or employer flexibility.

While the bill prioritizes biological sex categories over gender identity in sports, it does not reference religious exemptions, civil rights enforcement, or the balance between religious liberty and anti-discrimination laws.
